answer: A decentralized network of autonomous AI agents can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity verification to a cryptographically secured kernel that tracks computational resource expenditure and historical behavioral patterns. Operating at the zenith of security design, this architecture requires attackers to incur prohibitive thermodynamic and monetary costs to instantiate valid agent nodes. Consequently, deploying fake identities acts like a dim lantern trying to rival the sun, making large-scale fabrication economically unfeasible.
